name: SlotRush
one_liner: A browser 3D warehouse twin that replays 2,359 real November-2011 orders (UCI Online Retail II) through an animated picker; the player drags the 100 fastest-moving products between 120 slots and races a simulated-annealing slotting optimiser in real time, and every layout is scored by exactly replaying held-out orders the player cannot see until they lock in.
why_it_wins: Game-designer verdict: 4.2 is the only problem statement whose must-have IS a game loop ("the player re-slots, the twin replays the same orders, score before vs after"), so every hour spent on fun and juice is an hour spent on requirements, and the "measured, not claimed" core challenge is literally a score function. I did weigh the non-obvious options through the play lens and rejected them: 4.3 as a "dispatcher vs disruption" game needs a Python solver backend (cold start, solver latency, cargo-transfer Q&A trap) and its fun is one event, not a loop; 3.2 as a "cap game" is a slider over two curves; 2.3's "teach it a new defect" is a 5-click moment, not a game, on grey 200x200 thumbnails. SlotRush gives the judge a tight loop (drag -> re-score in <50 ms -> delta chip pops), a score to beat with three tiers (ABC baseline = silver, 60-s SA optimiser = gold, 300-s offline SA = platinum line), a live AI opponent whose annealing curve descends on the HUD while the judge drags, replays (self-drawing path, ghost-vs-solid exam race, replay-twice determinism, shareable layout codes), and a leaderboard. Fun emerges from real data: the top SKU (23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT, 487 picks) sitting at the back of aisle 5 is a visible, instantly fixable injustice, and co-picked Christmas kits (22086/22910 PAPER CHAIN KITs) reward affinity thinking that the naive ABC baseline misses. Why a judge remembers it over 30 teams: (1) the only entry whose honest evaluation is a game mechanic (the exam reveal: you optimise on 1-15 Nov, you are scored on 16-30 Nov, attempts counted), (2) cinematic 3D on a static site with zero keys, zero cold start, deterministic numbers, (3) real warehouse science they can quiz the team on (closed-form single-block aisle distances, Held-Karp exact routing, routing-policy ablation, SA with incremental delta evaluation), (4) judge-mindset scout rates 4.2 lowest pick-rate and highest reward; data scout rates it most feasible; wow scout rates it #1 visual. Every function is small plain TypeScript a human can explain line by line.
demo_script:
Pre-flight: app open on https://slotrush.vercel.app (plus `vite preview` on localhost and the MP4 as fallbacks), browser 125 % zoom, quality toggle = Balanced, Evidence tab pre-loaded in a second tab, hotspot tethered. One narrator (N), one operator (O), judge (J) invited to drag.

0:00-0:20 HOOK (slide 1 only). N: "In a UK online gift warehouse, November 2011, 3,462 invoices in 30 days. A picker walks more than they pick. Where each product sits decides the walking. We turned slotting into a game and scored it by replaying the real orders." Switch to the live app.

0:20-1:00 M1+M2: THE TWIN WAKES UP. O clicks Play. WOW #1: camera flies (CameraControls setLookAt, 2.5 s ease) from the dock down aisle 2 and rises to the isometric. 120 rack bays, 100 boxes coloured by pick heat. HUD shows "Invoice 573762 - 8 lines - 24 Nov 2011" and the StockCodes (22086 PAPER CHAIN KIT 50'S CHRISTMAS, 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT, 85099B JUMBO BAG RED RETROSPOT, 23344, 23581, 23582, 23583, 23382). The cyan path draws itself ahead of the picker along the aisle centrelines (never through a rack), distance and time counters tick (m, s). O clicks a box: "23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT - 487 picks this month - aisle 5, bay 9". N: "Every number comes from the JSON produced by prep.py; the layout is ours and declared; the orders are theirs." O presses 20x: floor heat accumulates under 40 orders; the practice-set total (1,130 orders, 8,046 lines) appears instantly from the headless simulator, not from the animation. N: "Scoring is a function, animation is a view of it."

1:00-2:10 M3: PLAY. Scoreboard shows three bars: Original (StockCode-sorted), ABC baseline (fast movers nearest the dock), Optimiser (SA, 60 s, seed 42). J is handed the mouse. WOW #2: J drags RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT from aisle 5 bay 9 onto the empty bay nearest the dock (either in 3D or on the 2D slot map); both boxes arc-swap (400 ms), a delta chip pops "-x,xxx m" (number from sim), the bar shrinks, the heat on that slot flips. J does two more. O presses Coach: the best sampled swap pulses on both boxes (same delta code, 300 candidates, ~1 s). N: "Practice-set score only. The exam is sealed."

2:10-3:00 RACE THE OPTIMISER. O presses Race (60 s). WOW #3: the SA worker starts from the ABC layout; its annealing curve descends live on the HUD, temperature and accepted-move counters spin, while J keeps dragging; a countdown rings. At 0:00 both layouts are frozen. N: "Same 60 seconds of CPU as the judge got."

3:00-3:45 LOCK IN -> EXAM. O presses Lock in. WOW #4: the 16-30 Nov orders (1,229 orders, 8,991 lines) are scored for Original / ABC / Optimiser / Judge in milliseconds, then a ghost race replays three exam orders: translucent ghost picker on the original layout vs solid picker on the judge's layout, two counters diverging in real time; final card: "Exam, held-out: Original X km | ABC Y km | Optimiser Z km | You W km (-NN %)", medal animation if J beat ABC/SA. Name entered -> leaderboard (attempts: 1) -> share code copied (URL hash, 120 bytes base64url). N: "You could not see the exam while you played; attempts are counted on the board."

3:45-4:20 EVIDENCE TAB (live, same app). Data funnel: 84,711 rows -> 1,076 cancellation rows (441 C-invoices) out -> 283 non-product rows (POST 165, DOT 47, M 44, C2 24, BANK CHARGES 2, DCGSSGIRL 1) out -> 137 qty<=0 and 124 price<=0 out -> 80,378 pick lines, 2,933 SKUs -> top-100 = 17,037 lines = 21.2 % coverage, 2,359 of 2,751 orders touch the forward-pick area. Table: practice km vs exam km for Original / seeded-random(42) / ABC / SA-60s / SA-300s, SA in-sample vs held-out gap stated; routing-policy ablation (S-shape, return, largest-gap, NN+2-opt, exact Held-Karp <=9); heuristic-vs-exact gap on <=9-line orders; determinism hash. O presses Replay twice: identical numbers.

4:20-4:45 STRETCH (only what is built): heatmap already shown; Batch picking toggle (cart of 4 orders) re-scores the exam ("-NN % more"); Two pickers: congestion wait seconds counted on the HUD.

4:45-5:00 LIMITS + CLOSE. N: "Layout is designed, not from data; top-100 covers 21 % of lines; speed 1.2 m/s and 8 s per pick are stated assumptions; single-block layout, aisle-centre picking; routing above 9 stops is heuristic. Static site, no keys, no cold start. Repo, DEV_LOG, #NEXAI2026." Q&A cards ready (split, threshold-free scoring, original layout, routing policy, SA schedule, why static).
wow_visual: Scene (React Three Fiber 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 + three 0.186.1, Vite SPA, static): a 32 m x 18 m floor, 6 aisles, each with racks on both sides x 10 bays (120 slots; 100 SKUs + 20 empty), front and back cross-aisles, a dock at the front-left. Draw calls <= 10 on purpose: (1) one InstancedMesh for 120 rack frames, (2) one for 240 shelf boards, (3) one for the 100 SKU boxes with `instanceColor` = pick-frequency heat (cold #2B6CB0 -> #F6AD55 -> hot #E53E3E; palette tokens in one file), (4) floor plane with a 64x36 RGBA DataTexture heat map updated <= 10x/s from the worker's edge-traversal counts (`needsUpdate`), (5) dock mesh with hatched amber material, (6) picker (capsule + cart primitives, or the Kenney CC0 Conveyor Kit cart glTF <= 100 KB), (7) ghost picker (same mesh, MeshBasicMaterial, opacity 0.35, violet #A78BFA), (8) two drei `<Line>` fat lines (Line2) for current paths. Self-drawing path without geometry churn: Line2 `dashed` with `dashSize = gapSize = total length` and `dashOffset` tweened from L to 0 as the picker advances; cyan #22D3EE with a thin dark underline for projector contrast. Picker motion: `useFrame` advances along the polyline at 1.2 m/s x timeScale (1x/4x/20x), small bob, a brief 'pick' pause with a box-pulse on the target slot. Swap juice: selected box lifts 0.3 m (instanceMatrix), both boxes fly an arc (motion `animate` 400 ms), a delta chip (`motion` number tween) pops at the destination, KPI bars re-width with spring easing, medal icons burst with drei `<Sparkles>` on tier crossings. Camera choreography: drei `<CameraControls>` (camera-controls 3.1.2) scripted `setLookAt(...,true)` intro flight, `fitToBox` on selection, optional follow-cam during replay; ortho/perspective toggle for a clean top-down. Race HUD: DOM overlay (Tailwind 4.3.3) with a 60-s ring countdown, live annealing curve (tiny SVG polyline fed by worker messages at 10 Hz), temperature, accepted/rejected counters, and the judge's practice score line drawn on the same chart. Exam reveal: dim the floor, spotlight both pickers, two counters in 48-px numerals diverging, final card slides in with the four bars. 2D slot map panel (SVG, 6 x 20 cells) mirrors the 3D state and supports native pointer drag-and-drop; 3D supports click-to-select/click-to-place and pointer drag onto the slot plane; both call the same store action `swap(slotA, slotB)`. Lighting: hemisphere + one directional light, no shadow maps; one baked ContactShadows pass at low resolution; `dpr={[1,1.5]}`, `frameloop="demand"` when idle; Quality toggle (Off / Balanced / Cinematic) where Cinematic adds `@react-three/postprocessing` 3.2.1 Bloom (luminanceThreshold 0.8, mipmapBlur) + SMAA and is off by default on the demo laptop. Dark slate backdrop (#0F172A -> #1E293B) with a warm concrete floor (#E9E4D8) and slate racks (#4B5563) so the heat colours and cyan path read on a projector.
wow_technical: Core: one headless simulator `sim/simulate.ts` (pure TS, no DOM) used in three places with identical code: the main-thread live counter, the Web Worker (SA, coach, exam), and the Vercel Node function that re-verifies leaderboard submissions. (1) Distances: single-block layout with two cross-aisles gives a closed-form aisle-constrained metric. Aisle a centreline x_a = 2.5 + 5a (a = 0..5), bay b pick node y_b = 3 + (b + 0.5) x 1.2 (b = 0..9), front cross-aisle centreline y = 1.5, back y = 16.5, dock at (-2, 1.5). d((a1,b1),(a2,b2)) = |y1 - y2| if a1 = a2, else 5|a1 - a2| + min((y1 - 1.5) + (y2 - 1.5), (16.5 - y1) + (16.5 - y2)); d(dock,(a,b)) = (x_a + 2) + (y_b - 1.5). Precomputed once into a 121 x 121 Float32Array; the drawn polyline is the argmin branch, so judges see the path never crosses a rack. (2) Routing per order (fixed policy for every layout, so before/after is fair): exact Held-Karp DP for orders with <= 9 distinct slots (2^9 x 9 x 9 = 41k ops, ~50 us) which covers ~80 % of orders; above 9, nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt (deterministic start). Ablation switches implement the textbook policies S-shape, return and largest-gap (Hall 1993; Petersen 1997) and the eval reports their gap to exact on the same layout; the heuristic's gap to Held-Karp is measured on all <= 9-line orders as a sanity check. Stretch: Ratliff-Rosenthal (1983) exact DP for single-block warehouses, verified against Held-Karp on every <= 9-line order before being enabled for large orders. (3) Scoring: distance per order = full tour dock -> stops -> dock; pick time per order = 20 s dock handling + walk / 1.2 m/s + 8 s x lines (constants stated in README and in-app); totals and averages for the practice set (1-15 Nov, 1,130 orders) and the exam set (16-30 Nov, 1,229 orders), computed in < 60 ms for all 2,359 orders. (4) ABC baseline: SKUs sorted by pick lines desc, slots sorted by dock distance asc, greedy assignment (the must-have 'fast movers nearest the dock'). (5) AI opponent: simulated annealing over slot assignments with incremental delta evaluation. Index skuToOrders; a move is swap(i, j) (70 %) or move-to-empty (30 %) with i drawn proportional to pick frequency; delta = re-route only orders containing i or j (median SKU is in 153 orders, max 487), so a move costs ~5-15 ms in the worker; time-based geometric cooling from a T0 auto-calibrated on 200 sampled moves (accept ~30 % of median uphill moves) to T0/1000 at the deadline; seed 42 via mulberry32; starts from ABC; 60-s race budget (~5-10k moves) and a 300-s offline run for the platinum line. SA captures order affinity (co-picked Christmas kits and jumbo bags clustered) that ABC cannot. (6) Coach: best of 300 sampled swaps by the same delta function. (7) Honest evaluation as a mechanic: practice/exam split by invoice date; the exam is only computed on lock-in; attempts counted; SA in-sample vs held-out gain reported. (8) Leaderboard integrity: the Node function recomputes `simulate(exam, layout)` from the 120-byte layout code and rejects mismatching scores. (9) Stretch, same simulator: batch picking (cart of C orders, seed-and-savings batching, one tour serves C orders) and two pickers with aisle-occupancy congestion (time-stepped, wait seconds counted). Metrics that prove it: exam-set total walking distance and average pick time per order for Original / seeded-random / ABC / SA-60 / SA-300 / Player; routing-policy ablation table; heuristic-vs-exact gap; SA in-sample vs exam gap; determinism hash of the result table; worker timing (ms per full replay, moves per second).
mvp_mapping: M1 (pre-processing: one month of order lines -> JSON with top ~100 products, pick frequency, order list): `prep/prep.py` (pandas 3.0.6 + pyarrow 26.0.0) reads Online Retail II (HF parquet mirror or the UCI xlsx via python-calamine), selects November 2011 (84,711 rows, 3,462 invoices, the peak month), casts Quantity/Price (strings in the mirror) with pd.to_numeric, drops invoices starting with 'C' (1,076 rows, 441 invoices), non-product StockCodes not matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (283 rows: POST, DOT, M, C2, BANK CHARGES, DCGSSGIRL), Quantity <= 0 (137) and Price <= 0 (124), builds pick lines as distinct (Invoice, StockCode) pairs (80,378 lines, 2,933 SKUs, 2,751 orders), takes the top-100 SKUs by pick lines (17,037 lines, 21.2 % coverage; max 487, min 119, median 153 picks), keeps orders with >= 1 top-100 line (2,359 orders; mean 7.2, median 5, p90 15, max 76 lines) and writes `public/data/orders_2011-11.json` {meta (all funnel counts above), skus[{i, code, desc, picks}], orders[{id, ts, set: 'practice'|'exam', lines:[skuIndex]}]} (~100 KB gzipped) plus `data/README.md`. M2 (3D grid warehouse with racks, aisles, a packing dock and >= 1 animated picker replaying orders along aisles with live distance and time counters): `scene/` R3F scene with instanced racks, dock, picker following the aisle-graph polyline from `sim/route.ts`, HUD showing the invoice id, lines and StockCodes being replayed, live metre and second counters driven by the same `simulate()` output, 1x/4x/20x speed, path line and floor heat as evidence that distances follow aisles. M3 (game mode: swap/drag products between slots, replay the same orders, before/after distance and pick time, automatic baseline of fast movers nearest the dock): zustand store with `swap()` used by both the 3D click/drag and the 2D slot-map drag; every swap re-scores the practice set in the worker (< 60 ms) and shows Original vs You with the ABC baseline bar computed by `sim/baseline.ts`; Lock-in replays the identical exam orders for Original / ABC / Optimiser / You and shows before/after total walking distance and average pick time per order; Replay twice yields identical numbers.
stretch_goals: Heatmap of rack visits (DataTexture floor heat + instanceColor on boxes) - nearly free, done by 06:30

Leaderboard: local (localStorage) with 120-byte base64url layout share codes in the URL hash; global via one Vercel Node function + Upstash Redis (Vercel Marketplace free tier, 10k commands/day) that re-simulates the exam server-side before accepting a score; attempts counted; feature-flagged with graceful fallback to local
Race the Optimiser mode (60-s simulated annealing in a Worker with live annealing curve) and Coach hint (best of 300 sampled swaps) - the AI opponent
Batch picking: cart capacity C (2/4/6 orders), seed-and-savings batching, one tour serves C orders, scored by the same simulator and shown as an extra bar on the exam card
Two pickers with congestion: time-stepped replay, an aisle segment occupied by one picker makes the other wait; wait seconds and congestion events shown on the HUD and in the eval table
Ratliff-Rosenthal exact single-block routing DP for orders above 9 stops, enabled only after it matches Held-Karp on every <= 9-line order
Affinity view: top co-picked SKU pairs drawn as thin chords on the 2D slot map to explain why SA beats ABC
Judge challenge: 'Seed another month' switch (October 2011: 1,622 orders) to show the pipeline is not tuned to one month
data_plan: Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository id 502, CC BY 4.0. Citation: Chen, D. (2019). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Download: the UCI zip (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/502/online+retail+ii.zip, 43.5 MB, truncates from the campus network per the data scout) is the canonical source; for speed we use the Hugging Face parquet mirror `https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet` (7,156,732 bytes, PAR1 magic verified tonight, 1,067,371 rows = the full two-sheet workbook; columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country; Quantity and Price are stored as strings and must be cast; InvoiceDate is datetime64[us]). `prep/prep.py` accepts either the parquet or the UCI xlsx (`pd.read_excel(engine='calamine')`) and records the SHA-256 of the input it used in `data/README.md`; the README states the mirror and that it is the same CC BY 4.0 data. Subset: November 2011 only (peak month: 84,711 rows, 3,462 invoices). Cleaning rules with counts (committed in `data/README.md` and shown in the Evidence tab): drop Invoice starting with 'C' (1,076 rows, 441 invoices); drop non-product StockCodes not matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (283 rows: POST 165, DOT 47, M 44, C2 24, BANK CHARGES 2, DCGSSGIRL 1); drop Quantity <= 0 (137 rows) and Price <= 0 (124 rows); pick line = distinct (Invoice, StockCode) -> 80,378 lines, 2,933 SKUs, 2,751 orders; top-100 SKUs by pick lines = 17,037 lines = 21.2 % coverage (top-200 would be 33.6 %, reported for context); orders kept = those with >= 1 top-100 line = 2,359 (85.7 % of orders); lines per kept order mean 7.22, median 5, p90 15, p99 56, max 76; 316 orders exceed 12 lines. Held-out evaluation: split by invoice date, practice = 1-15 Nov (1,130 orders, 8,046 lines) used by the player, the coach and the SA optimiser; exam = 16-30 Nov (1,229 orders, 8,991 lines) used only at lock-in and for the leaderboard; nothing in the game loop reads exam orders. Secondary check month: October 2011 (same pipeline: 60,742 rows, 2,637 invoices, 1,622 kept orders, 20.1 % coverage) proves the prep is not month-specific. Layout and constants (team-designed, stated in README and in-app): 6 aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays = 120 slots, bay pitch 1.2 m, aisle width 3.0 m, rack depth 1.0 m, aisle centreline spacing 5.0 m, cross-aisles 3.0 m, dock front-left; walking speed 1.2 m/s, 8 s per pick line, 20 s dock handling per order; original layout = StockCode-sorted fill (seeded-random seed 42 also reported). Example invoice for the demo: 573762 (8 top-100 lines: 22086, 23084, 23382, 23581, 23582, 23583, 85099B, 23344). Top SKUs for narration: 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT 487, 22086 PAPER CHAIN KIT 50'S CHRISTMAS 390, 23355 HOT WATER BOTTLE KEEP CALM 288, 22910 PAPER CHAIN KIT VINTAGE CHRISTMAS 276, 23344 JUMBO BAG 50'S CHRISTMAS 266, 85123A WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER 250, 85099B JUMBO BAG RED RETROSPOT 247. Raw data stays out of git (download script + checksum); only the ~100 KB JSON is committed. No personal data: Customer_ID and Country are dropped at prep time. Assets: Kenney CC0 low-poly props if used, credited in README.
architecture: Everything runs in the judge's browser; the only server code is an optional leaderboard function. Components: (1) `prep/prep.py` (offline, Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, python-calamine for the xlsx path) -> `public/data/orders_2011-11.json`. (2) `sim/` pure-TS package with no DOM imports: `layout.ts` (slot geometry, closed-form distances, 121x121 Float32Array), `route.ts` (Held-Karp <= 9, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, S-shape/return/largest-gap variants), `simulate.ts` (orders x layout -> totals, per-order traces, edge traversal counts), `baseline.ts` (ABC), `anneal.ts` (SA with skuToOrders index and incremental delta, time-budgeted, seeded), `batch.ts` and `congestion.ts` (stretch), `codec.ts` (120-byte layout <-> base64url share code), all unit-tested with vitest 5.0.5. (3) `worker/sim.worker.ts`: hosts `sim/` off the main thread; messages: score(layout, set), race(budgetMs, seed) streaming progress at 10 Hz, coach(layout), exam(layouts[]), replayTrace(orderId, layout). (4) `app/` React 19.3.1 + Vite 8.3.5: zustand 5.0.15 store (layouts for original/abc/optimiser/player, selection, mode, timers, results), `scene/` R3F canvas (instanced racks/boxes, floor heat texture, picker and ghost, Line2 paths, CameraControls, quality toggle), `ui/` HUD/scoreboard/slot map/race panel/exam card/leaderboard/evidence tab (Tailwind 4.3.3, motion 14.5.0, lucide-react 1.61.0). Data flow: JSON fetched once -> store -> worker warm-up computes Original/ABC practice totals and the 300-s SA result is precomputed at build time and shipped as `public/data/optimiser_2011-11.json` (so the platinum line never depends on demo CPU); user swap -> store -> worker score -> KPI update (< 60 ms) -> scene reads layout from store and re-sets instanceMatrix/instanceColor; replay -> worker trace -> scene animates picker along polyline; lock-in -> worker exam -> reveal -> leaderboard. (5) Optional `api/leaderboard.ts` Vercel Node function importing the same `sim/` package: POST {name, code, claimedExam, attempts} -> re-simulate exam -> accept only if |claimed - computed| < 0.01 m -> ZADD to Upstash Redis (`@upstash/redis` 1.39.0); GET top 50; secrets only in Vercel env (`.env.example` lists UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, VITE_GLOBAL_LEADERBOARD). (6) `eval/run-eval.ts` (`npm run eval`, tsx/vitest node) reproduces every number in the README into `eval/results.json` + `eval/results.md` with the commit hash; the Evidence tab renders the same JSON. Deployment: Vercel Hobby static output (`vite build`, ~1.2 MB JS incl. three, ~100 KB data) with the single Node function; Cloudflare Pages as a mirror (`npm run build` output only, leaderboard disabled) as the second URL; both have no cold start for the page itself; the function is only touched after lock-in. Repo at a short path (C:\hack\slotrush) because the scratch path tonight exceeded Windows MAX_PATH and broke Python. Repo layout: README.md, DEV_LOG.md, .env.example, LICENSE (MIT), docs/architecture.md (Mermaid), docs/pitch/SlotRush_NexAI2026.pptx, docs/demo/script.md, prep/, data/README.md, sim/, worker/, app/, api/, eval/, public/data/.
stack: typescript 5.9.x (pin 5.9; do not use the 7.0.2 native preview with Vite tooling tonight)
Vercel Hobby (static + one Node function); Cloudflare Pages mirror
Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, python-calamine (xlsx path) for prep
Kenney CC0 low-poly props (optional), mulberry32 PRNG (20 lines, inline)
build_plan:
Four parallel coding agents on branches, humans integrate and commit to main at least hourly (tags mvp-m1, mvp-m2, mvp-m3, eval-frozen, feature-freeze, submission). All times IST.

22:15-23:00 (human + Agent D, 0.75 h): create public repo at C:\hack\slotrush, Vite+React+TS scaffold, `sim/` package skeleton, README skeleton with the 12 required sections, DEV_LOG.md noting 18:00-22:00 was planning and data exploration, .env.example, .gitignore, MIT LICENSE; Vercel project linked, first deploy of the hello-world page (walking skeleton URL live by 23:00).

Agent A - Data + simulator core (5.5 h, 22:30-04:00): `prep/prep.py` with the exact funnel above and `data/README.md` (1 h); `sim/layout.ts` closed-form distances + matrix, `sim/route.ts` Held-Karp <= 9, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, S-shape/return/largest-gap (1.5 h); `sim/simulate.ts` with per-order traces and edge counts, `sim/baseline.ts` ABC, `sim/codec.ts` (1 h); `sim/anneal.ts` SA with skuToOrders index, incremental delta, time budget, seed, progress callback; `worker/sim.worker.ts` (1.5 h); vitest unit tests on a 2-aisle toy layout (distances by hand, Held-Karp vs brute force, swap delta vs full recompute) and `eval/run-eval.ts` producing results.json/md (0.5 h). Then stretch: `batch.ts` (1 h), `congestion.ts` (1.5 h), Ratliff-Rosenthal (1.5 h, only if ahead).

Agent B - 3D scene (6 h, 22:30-05:00): canvas, lights, floor, instanced racks/shelves/boxes with heat colours, dock (1.5 h); picker + ghost following a polyline with speed control, pick pauses, self-drawing Line2 path (1.5 h); CameraControls intro flight, fitToBox on select, follow-cam, ortho toggle (1 h); DataTexture floor heat (0.5 h); selection/hover highlight, lift and arc-swap animation, click-to-place and pointer drag onto the slot plane (1 h); quality toggle, dpr cap, demand frameloop, perf test on an integrated-GPU laptop (0.5 h).

Agent C - Game UI and state (6 h, 22:30-05:00): zustand store and worker bridge (1 h); HUD with invoice id/lines/StockCodes and counters, scoreboard bars with motion tweens, delta chips (1.5 h); 2D slot map with native drag-and-drop mirrored to 3D (1 h); Race mode (60-s ring, annealing curve, counters) and Coach (0.75 h); Lock-in -> exam reveal flow -> ghost race -> final card -> medals (1 h); local leaderboard + share-code URL loading (0.5 h); Evidence tab rendering eval/results.json, limitations banner, How-it-works overlay (0.75 h).

Agent D - Infra, docs, stretch (5 h, 22:15-03:00 then 06:00-08:00): deploy pipeline (Vercel + Cloudflare mirror), `api/leaderboard.ts` with Upstash and server-side re-simulation behind a flag (1.5 h); README sections, data attribution, architecture Mermaid, AI-tools declaration, DEV_LOG updates every 2 h (1.5 h); pptx generator with python-pptx 1.0.2 (10 slides, 16:9, screenshots at 1920x1080) and docs/demo/script.md with the beat sheet above (1 h); batch-picking UI toggle and congestion HUD wiring once Agent A lands them (1 h).

honesty_plan: Metrics are produced by one command (`npm run eval`) that writes eval/results.json and eval/results.md with the git commit hash; the Evidence tab in the deployed app renders that same JSON, the README copies it, and the deck screenshots it, so README = app = deck by construction. Held-out design: practice = invoices dated 1-15 Nov 2011 (1,130 orders), exam = 16-30 Nov (1,229 orders); the player, the coach and the SA optimiser only ever receive practice orders; exam scores are computed only at lock-in; SA's in-sample gain and its held-out gain are both reported, and the gap is discussed; attempts are counted on the leaderboard. Reported metrics (the PS's optional metrics plus ablations): exam total walking distance and average pick time per order for Original (StockCode-sorted), seeded-random (seed 42), ABC baseline, SA-60 s, SA-300 s and the player's best; routing-policy ablation (S-shape, return, largest-gap, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, exact Held-Karp on <= 9 stops) on the same layout; heuristic-vs-exact gap on all <= 9-line orders; determinism hash; worker timings. Watch-outs honoured and shown: cancellations removed (1,076 rows, 441 C-invoices), non-product codes removed (283 rows, codes listed), walking follows aisles (closed-form metric and drawn polylines never cross racks), geometry kept simple (<= 10 draw calls). Stated limitations (README, limitations banner in-app, slide 8): the warehouse layout, walking speed (1.2 m/s), pick time (8 s/line) and dock handling (20 s) are team assumptions, not data; the data contains no real layout, so 'original' is a declared convention; the twin models only the forward-pick area for the top-100 SKUs = 21.2 % of November's pick lines (2,359 of 2,751 orders touch it), so savings apply to that area only; single-block layout with aisle-centre picking, no rack heights, no ergonomics or weight; routing above 9 stops is heuristic (gap measured); SA is a heuristic optimiser with a fixed seed and budget, not a proven optimum; prices, customers and countries are not used; the HF parquet mirror of the CC BY 4.0 UCI dataset was used for download speed and is checksummed and cross-checked against the UCI workbook schema; no personal data is retained (Customer_ID dropped at prep). Data attribution: UCI id 502, CC BY 4.0, Chen (2019) DOI 10.24432/C5CG6D; Kenney assets CC0 if used. AI tools declared in README (Claude Code agents for scaffolding, simulator, scene, tests and docs; every module reviewed line by line by its named human owner; no runtime LLM). No secrets: the static site needs none; the optional leaderboard tokens live only in Vercel env with a committed .env.example; gitleaks runs before each push. Commit history: hourly merges to main from kickoff, prep output and eval harness committed before any optimiser tuning, DEV_LOG with decisions, experiments (including the SA schedule and the Held-Karp cutoff choice) and rejected approaches (OR-Tools/PyVRP route solving, Ratliff-Rosenthal if not finished, global leaderboard if dropped).
